Hi Aimee — thanks, great convo yesterday. Attaching a concise trial runbook and an acceptance-tests workbook that maps each success metric to a measurable test, owner, and pass/fail threshold. High-level highlights below:

1) Success metrics (primary):
- End-to-end task accuracy >= 88% on curated clinical triage prompts (sample set in sheet 'baseline').
- 95th percentile generation latency <= 80ms under stated concurrency profile (we can tighten if you need <50ms; see caveat).
- No high-severity hallucination incidents in 500 random cases (severity rubric in workbook).

2) Exit gates (fail-fast / go criteria):
- Immediate stop: any safety or PHI leak discovered during smoke tests.
- Pause and remediate: sustained P95 latency regression of >25% for 48+ hours.
- Go / proceed to procurement signoff: all acceptance tests green for two consecutive daily runs and stakeholder signoff (Clinical + Security).

3) Acceptance tests (samples in acceptance-tests.xlsx):
- Functional: 100 representative prompts, pass if >=88% match to oracle labels.
- Latency: scripted load-run under 40 concurrent sessions, measure p95 tokens.
- Safety: adversarial prompt sweep (50 cases) — no high/critical severity responses.

Attachments: trial-map_v1.pdf (MAP one-pager), acceptance-tests.xlsx (detailed test cases), sla-addendum.docx (draft language).

Notes on latency: our hosted tier can meet p95 <=80ms for the described model/sequence mix. Hitting a sustained <50ms p95 requires dedicated capacity + custom quantization and network colocations (we can outline the dedicated plan as an opt-in).

Proposed schedule:
- Thu 3/31: technical walkthrough + test owners meeting
- Week 1 (4/1–4/7): baseline data collection and smoke runs
- Week 2–3: acceptance test runs and instrumentation
- Week 4: final verification and procurement signoff (if all green)

If that looks good I'll publish the MAP to a shared Drive and send a DocuSign for the MAP acceptance block.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Ben / Grace — forwarding Aimee's ask + the MAP I just sent. Quick internal plan and risks:

- Ownering: Ben (latency/infra), Grace (safety & test design), Jordan (canary config + dedicated capacity options).
- Risks: MedPrompt's baseline has long sequences in ~20% of samples — will inflate latency. Recommend we instrument prefix caching and limit max_tokens during acceptance runs to reflect production.
- Contingency: if p95 can't reach 80ms with hosted, we propose a 2-week dedicated evaluation window; cost estimate in the SLA doc.

Action items:
1) Ben: prepare a lightweight canary config and a cost delta for 2-week dedicated (due EOD tomorrow).
2) Grace: review the safety sweep cases in the workbook and add 10 additional edge prompts by EOD (clinical reviewer names).
3) Jordan: prep the routing policy that will pin requests to the canary pool for acceptance tests.

I'll send the Drive link once Aimee confirms. Keep replies internal until we lock the procurement language.

—Mina
